title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 12
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Regional cost index, where the national figure is 100:

North: 108
East: 68
South: 124
West: 97
Central: 103

Which region's index is furthest from the national figure?
questions.explanation: Distance from 100: North 8, East 32, South 24, West 3, Central 3. East is furthest at 32 below. South has the highest index in the table but sits only 24 above the national figure, so "highest" and "furthest from average" are different questions.

questions.prompt:
Units sold of two products:

2020: Product A 1,200, Product B 380
2021: Product A 1,050, Product B 560
2022: Product A 900, Product B 810
2023: Product A 760, Product B 990
2024: Product A 640, Product B 1,240

In which year do sales of Product B first exceed sales of Product A?
options: E. Product B never overtakes Product A
questions.explanation: The gap closes each year: 2020 820, 2021 490, 2022 90, 2023 -230, 2024 -600. In 2022 B is still 90 behind, and 2023 is the first year it is ahead, by 230.

questions.prompt:
Group sizes and their mean scores:

Group 1: 40 people, mean 62
Group 2: 75 people, mean 72
Group 3: 25 people, mean 84
Group 4: 60 people, mean 58

What is the mean score across all 200 people?
questions.explanation: Weight each mean by its group size: 40 × 62 + 75 × 72 + 25 × 84 + 60 × 58 = 13,460, over 200 people: 67.3. Averaging the four means without weighting gives 69, which lets the 25-person group count as much as the 75-person one.

questions.prompt:
Eight readings, in order: 34, 38, 41, 41, 45, 47, 50, 52

A ninth reading of 12 is then added. Which statement about the effect is accurate?
options: A. The mode falls along with the mean
D. The mean falls but the median rises
E. The mean and the median both fall, the mode is unchanged, and the range more than doubles
questions.explanation: Before: mean 43.5, median 43, mode 41, range 18. After: mean 40, median 41, mode 41, range 40. A single low value drags the mean down hardest, moves the median by one place, leaves the repeated 41 untouched, and stretches the range from 18 to 40.

questions.prompt:
12 workers build a wall in 21 days, all working at the same rate.

Select the number of days 18 workers would take AND the number of workers needed to finish in 9 days.
options: A. 14 days with 18 workers; 24 workers for 9 days
B. 16 days with 18 workers; 28 workers for 9 days
C. 14 days with 18 workers; 28 workers for 9 days
D. 31.5 days with 18 workers; 28 workers for 9 days
E. Neither figure can be worked out from what is given
questions.explanation: The job is 12 × 21 = 252 worker-days however it is staffed. Spread over 18 workers that is 14 days; squeezed into 9 days it needs 28 workers. More workers means fewer days, so 14 must come out below 21, not above.

questions.prompt:
Partner P invests GBP 15,000.00 for 12 months and Partner Q invests GBP 24,000.00 for 10 months. Profit of GBP 35,000.00 is shared in proportion to capital multiplied by the time it was invested.

Select each partner's share.
questions.explanation: The weights are GBP 15,000.00 × 12 = 180,000 and GBP 24,000.00 × 10 = 240,000, a ratio of 3 : 4. Splitting GBP 35,000.00 that way gives GBP 15,000.00 and GBP 20,000.00. Sharing by capital alone would give P GBP 13,461.54 and ignore the two extra months.

questions.prompt:
Output and unit cost on two production lines:

Line One: 24,000 units at GBP 3.80 each
Line Two: 7,500 units at GBP 5.60 each

Select the line with the lower cost per unit AND the line with the lower total cost.
options: A. Line One on both measures
B. Line Two on both measures
C. Line Two on cost per unit; Line One on total cost
D. The two lines are equal on both measures
E. Line One on cost per unit; Line Two on total cost
questions.explanation: Unit costs are given: Line One GBP 3.80, Line Two GBP 5.60. Totals are Line One GBP 91,200.00 and Line Two GBP 42,000.00. The cheaper line per unit runs more than three times the volume, so it costs far more in total — the two measures do not agree.

questions.prompt:
A student has scored 68, 74, 61, 79 on four papers. A fifth paper remains.

Select the score needed on the fifth paper for an average of 72 AND whether a score of 100 would lift the average above 76.
options: E. The average of 72 cannot be reached
questions.explanation: The four papers total 282, and five papers averaging 72 must total 360, so the fifth must score 78. A 100 would bring the total to 382, an average of 76.4 — above 76, though only just.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): donations received — Charity A GBP 1,240,000.00, Charity B GBP 480,000.00, Charity C GBP 2,900,000.00

SOURCE 2 (table): administrative costs — Charity A GBP 186,000.00, Charity B GBP 62,400.00, Charity C GBP 319,000.00

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The grant goes to whichever charity spends the smallest share of its donations on administration."

Which charity receives the grant?
options: C. The three charities are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Administration as a share of donations: Charity A 15.0%, Charity B 13.0%, Charity C 11.0%. Charity C is lowest, and it is also much the largest charity. Charity B spends the least on administration in cash terms but takes in far less, so its share is higher.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "The average wait fell from 47 minutes to 29 minutes."

SOURCE 2 (note): "From January the waiting clock starts at triage rather than at arrival."

SOURCE 3 (table): the average time between arrival and triage is 21 minutes.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Patients are now seen 18 minutes sooner than before
B. Triage now takes 21 minutes longer than it used to
C. Most of the fall reflects a period that is no longer counted rather than a shorter wait
D. Waiting times rose once the change is accounted for
E. The change in measurement had no effect on the reported figure
questions.explanation: The reported fall is 18 minutes, and the stretch removed from the measure averages 21 minutes — more than the whole improvement. That accounts for the headline without any patient being seen sooner. It does not prove waits rose, because the sources do not say what happened after triage.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): price per copy — Printer A GBP 0.04, Printer B GBP 0.06, Printer C GBP 0.05

SOURCE 2 (table): lead time — Printer A 14 working days, Printer B 6 working days, Printer C 9 working days

SOURCE 3 (email): "We need 12,000 copies delivered within 10 working days, at the lowest cost."

Which printer should be used?
options: D. All three cost the same
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Printer A is cheapest per copy but quotes 14 working days, past the deadline. Of the two that can deliver in time, Printer B costs GBP 660.00 and Printer C costs GBP 576.00, so Printer C wins. The deadline decides the shortlist before price decides the winner.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (survey): "At least 60% of respondents named cost as a barrier."

SOURCE 2 (table): 38% named lack of time.

SOURCE 3 (note): respondents could name more than one barrier; 1,400 people replied.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. At least 840 respondents named cost
C. 98% named either cost or lack of time
D. Fewer than half of respondents named cost
questions.explanation: 60% of 1,400 is 840, and source 1 says at least that share, so 840 is a floor rather than a count. The percentages cannot be added, because source 3 says one person could name both, so any figure for "cost or time" or for the overlap is beyond the sources.

questions.prompt:
How many pages are there in a book?

(1) Reading 24 pages a day finishes it in exactly 15 days.
(2) Reading 30 pages a day finishes it in fewer than 13 days.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) fixes the length at 24 times 15, which is 360 pages. (2) only says the total is under 390, which fits 360 but also 380 and many other figures. The two are consistent, since 360 pages at 30 a day would take 12 days.

questions.prompt:
What is the average weekly wage at a firm?

(1) The total weekly wage bill is GBP 48,000.
(2) More than 200 people work there.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: The average is the bill divided by the headcount. (1) gives the bill but no headcount, and (2) gives only a lower bound, so 240 staff would mean GBP 200 each and 400 staff would mean GBP 120. Even together the two leave the figure open, because "more than 200" is not a number.

questions.prompt:
What is the value of 2x + 6?

(1) x + 3 = 11
(2) 4x = 32
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives x = 8, so 2x + 6 = 22; it can also be read straight off, since 2x + 6 is twice (x + 3), which is twice 11. (2) gives x = 8 as well, so 2x + 6 = 22 again. Each statement alone settles it, and the two agree.

questions.prompt:
What was a shop's profit last month?

(1) Revenue was GBP 84,000.
(2) Costs came to 65% of revenue.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) gives revenue but no costs, and (2) gives costs only as a proportion of an unknown revenue. Together, profit is the remaining 35% of GBP 84,000, which is GBP 29,400. Both statements are needed and both are used.

questions.prompt:
Which factory produces the most units for each person on its workforce?

Factory | Lines | Units a year | Defects per 10,000 | Workforce
Ashford | 6 | 480,000 | 34 | 160
Brackley | 3 | 165,000 | 61 | 95
Cranwell | 9 | 918,000 | 22 | 340
Denby | 5 | 310,000 | 47 | 165
Eastleigh | 7 | 623,000 | 51 | 245
Fenwick | 4 | 236,000 | 53 | 128
questions.explanation: Units divided by workforce: Ashford 3,000, Brackley 1,737, Cranwell 2,700, Denby 1,879, Eastleigh 2,543, Fenwick 1,844. Ashford is highest at 3,000. Cranwell makes far more units in total but employs more than twice as many people to do it.

questions.prompt:
Which factory turns out the most defective units in a year?

Factory | Lines | Units a year | Defects per 10,000 | Workforce
Ashford | 6 | 480,000 | 34 | 160
Brackley | 3 | 165,000 | 61 | 95
Cranwell | 9 | 918,000 | 22 | 340
Denby | 5 | 310,000 | 47 | 165
Eastleigh | 7 | 623,000 | 51 | 245
Fenwick | 4 | 236,000 | 53 | 128
questions.explanation: Defective units are output multiplied by the rate per ten thousand: Ashford 1,632, Brackley 1,007, Cranwell 2,020, Denby 1,457, Eastleigh 3,177, Fenwick 1,251. Eastleigh is highest, without having either the largest output — that is Cranwell — or the worst rate, which is Brackley at 61. It ranks only second on output and third on defect rate, but no other factory is high on both, and the product is what counts.

questions.prompt:
How many factories each produce more than 15% of the six-factory total?

Factory | Lines | Units a year | Defects per 10,000 | Workforce
Ashford | 6 | 480,000 | 34 | 160
Brackley | 3 | 165,000 | 61 | 95
Cranwell | 9 | 918,000 | 22 | 340
Denby | 5 | 310,000 | 47 | 165
Eastleigh | 7 | 623,000 | 51 | 245
Fenwick | 4 | 236,000 | 53 | 128
questions.explanation: The six make 2,732,000 units between them, so 15% is 409,800. Above it: Ashford 480,000, Cranwell 918,000, Eastleigh 623,000 — 3 factories. 310,000 at Denby is the nearest miss.

questions.prompt:
How many factories are above the median on units per worker and below the median on defect rate?

Factory | Lines | Units a year | Defects per 10,000 | Workforce
Ashford | 6 | 480,000 | 34 | 160
Brackley | 3 | 165,000 | 61 | 95
Cranwell | 9 | 918,000 | 22 | 340
Denby | 5 | 310,000 | 47 | 165
Eastleigh | 7 | 623,000 | 51 | 245
Fenwick | 4 | 236,000 | 53 | 128
questions.explanation: The medians are 2210.82 units per worker and 49 defects per ten thousand. Above on output per worker: Ashford, Cranwell, Eastleigh. Below on defect rate: Ashford, Cranwell, Denby. On both counts: Ashford, Cranwell — 2. The two lists overlap only partly, so productivity and quality do not travel together here.
